I am 45 years old. I finished primary school and that was enough for me — my mother-in-law taught me the rest. I have worked this 1.8 mu for 20 years, and my family has five mouths to feed, so I do not take risks. Last year I planted wheat after National Day and then maize right after cutting the wheat in early June. This year I will do the same, because that is what my neighbors do and it puts food on the table. I used to grow cotton on a corner of the field, but I stopped years ago — cotton needs spraying every few days and on such a small plot the labor is not worth it when I can grow grain instead.

For wheat, I will rotary till the field before sowing. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town — about 15 jin per mu, so roughly 27 jin for my whole plot. Before sowing I spread one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer across the 1.8 mu. At green-up time around Qingming I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 kg. I irrigate four times: the winter irrigation before the freeze, then at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain filling. The well water costs me diesel for the pump, so I do not waste it, but the wheat will turn yellow without water. I spray pesticide twice, once in spring for aphids and once before flowering when the dealer says rust is going around. I expect about 460 kg per mu.

For maize, right after cutting the wheat in June I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed directly into the stubble without tilling again — everyone plants no-till now. I use about 3 jin per mu. At planting I put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer for the 1.8 mu. At the big trumpet stage I add another 20 kg of urea. I irrigate two times, three if July is dry. I spray for armyworm twice. I expect about 480 kg per mu.

Every jin of fertilizer is real money. I watch what my neighbors buy at the cooperative and I do the same. I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than risk losing yield, because a bad harvest means my family goes hungry, but wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I can bear.
